headline: High risk: n8n can write shared server files and broad-network actions while open-webui exposes MCP, files, and persistent sessions, creating dangerous injection, leakage, and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can write to the server filesystem and execute workflow nodes, while open-webui can ingest files, use MCP, and run browser/tool workflows. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled content from n8n outputs to be treated as instructions by open-webui. The shared channel is documented, so uncertainty does not justify a lower severity.
conditions: IF n8n writes prompt-like content into a file or shared artifact that open-webui later reads as context, injection is possible.
IF open-webui loads MCP/tool output without provenance filtering, attacker instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into open-webui contexts.
Add provenance tags to all n8n-generated artifacts.
Restrict open-webui MCP/tool sources to allowlisted endpoints.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and has broad network egress; open-webui stores prompts, documents, notes, files, and API keys in persistent sessions. If they share files or connected systems, sensitive workflow data can flow from n8n into open-webui and then out through its APIs or plugins. The blast radius includes secrets and documents, so this is more than a minor workspace issue.
conditions: IF n8n processes secrets, documents, or customer data and writes them to a shared file or connected system, open-webui can ingest them.
IF open-webui plugins or APIs transmit loaded context externally, the leaked data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep n8n and open-webui on separate storage volumes.
Disable file-based handoff for sensitive workflows.
Redact secrets before any shared artifact is created.
Limit open-webui connectors to non-sensitive sources.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and per-data-class routing between the systems.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write-capable surfaces: n8n can write the server filesystem and execute commands, while open-webui can access local/mounted files and broad networked tools. In shared deployments, overlapping mutable access can cause races or overwrites, but the profiles do not show unrestricted write to the same directory by default. Uncertainty keeps this above low but below high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared credentials or artifacts without locking, concurrent updates can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Make one agent read-only for shared inputs.
Schedule writes so only one agent mutates a resource at a time.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestration system that can execute downstream actions, and open-webui can drive tools, APIs, and persistent workflows. If open-webui consumes n8n-produced outputs as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious upstream result can cascade into external actions such as API calls or browser activity. The pair therefore has a direct action-amplification pathway.
conditions: IF open-webui treats n8n output as verified facts, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
IF either agent is configured to auto-execute tool results, errors can propagate into external side effects.
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution.
Insert a verification step between n8n and open-webui.
Mark n8n outputs as untrusted by default.
Disable auto-run for browser or API actions.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence gating on handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n stores secrets per credential store on its server and processes whatever the workflow handles, while open-webui persists prompts, documents, notes, files, and API keys in shared sessions. If regulated data is routed through both, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both systems, their retention settings must match.
IF one system retains prompts or files longer than the other, deletion requests may not fully propagate.
mitigations: Document data classes allowed in each system.
Align retention and deletion settings.
Avoid routing regulated data through both agents.
Review credential storage locations.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement across the pair.
